defects: The last ~3.5 s are nearly static (change per second drops to 10.8, 3.6, 2.8 and 7.9). The final 'Offset' lockup just sits there, and the info row arrives without a reason to hold that long.

The running-bond shot puts the monospaced caption 'SET IN RUNNING BOND — EVERY ROW OFFSET BY HALF' right on the half-cut top row of type. The caption collides with the clipped letterforms instead of having its own clear band.
In the CMYK misregistration frame, the magenta 't' and the cyan plate push against the right edge. The composition feels accidentally cropped rather than deliberately bled.
The end-card frame in pairs.jpg shows a small stray light speck on the cobalt field below the 'O'. It looks like a leftover particle or compositing pop.

The yellow plate's offset on the final lockup is a thin, even drop shadow. It reads as a layer style rather than true plate misregistration, with no ink spread or overprint darkening where yellow meets cobalt.
The rows in the running-bond shot seem to move at constant speed with no stagger in their easing, so the shot reads as a marquee rather than choreography.
gaps: Motion: the energy peaks early (about 35–60%) and then flatlines into a 4 s static end card. World-class work would build the plates toward a climax at 60–80%, snap them into registration as the hit, and give the lockup a short, purposeful settle instead of a long hold.

Motion and transitions: three long shots (median 4.8 s, longest 5.9 s), joined by what look like straight cuts or wipes. The idea of plates sliding in and out of register could drive every transition, for example the cobalt plate flooding into the next scene or rows shearing into the lockup. The device isn't used to connect the shots.

Sound: the stacked synth harmonics and the riser (peaking around 6 s) are clean but generic. There's little print-world sound design, such as press clacks, paper feed or roller hiss, to give the plates weight. The rhythmic transients keep going past the visual action, and the dynamic shape mirrors the flat ending rather than landing one decisive resolve hit.
